title: 2001 AMC 12 Problem 2
statement: Let \(P(n)\) and \(S(n)\) denote the product and the sum, respectively, of the digits of the integer \(n.\) For example, \(P(23) = 6\) and \(S(23) = 5.\) Suppose \(N\) is a two-digit number such that \(N = P(N) + S(N).\) What is the units digit of \(N?\)

solutions.text:
Write \(N = 10a + b.\) Then \(P(N) = ab\) and \(S(N) = a + b,\) so \[ 10a + b = ab + a + b. \] This reduces to \(9a = ab.\) Since \(a \neq 0,\) we can divide by \(a\) to get \(b = 9.\)

The units digit of \(N\) is \(9.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Write \(N = 10a + b\) where \(a\) is the tens digit and \(b\) is the units digit
The equation \(10a + b = ab + a + b\) simplifies to \(9a = ab\)
